Hello Meera,
You are in "Client sync: Patient Booking App" on 2026-10-20 at 08:30. Here is what to settle with the client so the requirements are fixed before the work moves on.

Questions to settle:
1. Which group should try Patient Booking App first? Get a named group and agree it. (memory item I0350)
2. Do we have the final brand colours and fonts? If not, who sends them and by when? (memory item I0422)
3. Which screens must work offline? The four-hour offline rule is decided, but the screen list is still open. (memory item I0483)
4. Who are the people for each user role? Agree the list so access rules can be frozen. (memory item I0349)
5. Has the marketing team reviewed the list of twelve events to track? Confirm the list is final. (memory item I0485)
6. What is the status of the WhatsApp business account approval, and what is the new launch plan if Meta is late again? (memory item I0286)
7. Which dates go into the shared plan now that launch has moved to 20 November? (memory item I0310)
8. Has the client tested the latest build, and when will they send comments? This task has been open since June. (memory item I0202, I0229, I0446)
9. When is the next review, and which demo build is ready for it? (memory item I0205, I0311, I0390)

Decisions that changed since last time:
- Changed on 2026-10-10: We decided that the first clinic launch is on 6 November → the launch will be on 20 November. (Source: Quick catch-up: MedBridge, 2026-10-10, line 4)

Open requirements:
- Hindi screens for patients are still open and the client says they need them. (Source: Client sync: MedBridge booking app, 2026-09-30, line 5; Sprint review: MedBridge booking app 2, 2026-08-11, line 4; Growth call 2: MedBridge proposal, 2026-05-25, line 2)
- A weekly reports dashboard for clinic admins. (Source: Client sync: MedBridge booking app 2, 2026-10-07, line 3)
- Lab results shown in the app, from the client's lab. (Source: Client sync: MedBridge booking app 2, 2026-10-07, line 4)
- Patients upload an insurance claim with a photo. The client asked about progress on 30 September. (Source: Sprint review: MedBridge booking app, 2026-07-14, line 2; SOW change SC12, 2026-08-17, line 1)
- Reminders on WhatsApp, not SMS. This depends on the WhatsApp approval. (Source: Sprint review: MedBridge booking app 2, 2026-08-11, line 2)

Blockers:
- The WhatsApp approval has not come. We are waiting for the reply from Meta. (Source: Quick catch-up: MedBridge, 2026-10-10, line 2)

Commitments due:
- DevX said it would send the estimate for the claim upload change by the next day. Check that the client received it. (Source: Sprint review: MedBridge booking app, 2026-07-14, line 6)

Statements that conflict:
- The launch moved from 6 November to 20 November. The client's first request was before Diwali, in the first week of November. A late approval is a risk to the new date. (Source: Quick catch-up: MedBridge, 2026-10-10, line 4; Growth call: MedBridge patient app, 2026-05-22, line 7; Quick catch-up: MedBridge, 2026-10-10, line 6)

Recent decisions:
- Launch will be on 20 November. (Source: Quick catch-up: MedBridge, 2026-10-10, line 4)
- Reminders will go by WhatsApp only. (Source: Client sync: MedBridge booking app, 2026-09-30, line 14)

Watch out for:
- The launch date moved from 6 November to 20 November. Confirm the client accepts 20 November. Their first request was before Diwali, in the first week of November.
- The WhatsApp approval from Meta has not come. If it is late again, the launch is at risk. Reminders are decided as WhatsApp only, so there is no SMS fallback.
- The Hindi patient screens are still open. The client has asked for them several times, and they asked again about Hindi translations on 30 September.
- The client asked about the insurance claim flow, the weekly reports dashboard, lab results in the app and support contacts. Agree scope and owner for each before the project moves on.
- Early SOW changes removed the clinic admin panel from phase one. A later request asks for a weekly reports dashboard for clinic admins. Confirm whether the dashboard is in or out of phase one.
- The label printer decision (phase two) has no linked question. Check that the client agrees.
- One brain item is unconfirmed. Do not treat everything as settled.
- The same tasks (test feedback, demo build, meeting notes) were logged several times since June. Close the old ones.
- I did not read recent client Slack messages for this brief.

Settle the pilot group, brand assets, offline screen list, user roles and the analytics event list. Confirm the new 20 November launch date against the WhatsApp approval risk. Close the Hindi screens, insurance claims, reports dashboard and lab results requirements, and get each one agreed and frozen.

letters.text:
Deal brief: CareNest Clinics (closing)
CareNest Clinics (healthcare, closing, INR 42 lakh) has twelve clinics in three cities and wants a patient booking app on mobile. All items for this deal are confirmed. The two objections are price and data storage. The client is unhappy with the price, and the budget of INR 40 lakh is below the deal value. Use the paid pilot at three clinics, which the client suggested and likes, to answer price. Give a clear written answer on data storage. At kickoff, ask the seven checklist questions, because past healthcare projects added these requirements late.

Ideas to close:
- Give a clear, written answer on where patient data will be stored before the client asks again. Put it in the proposal. (I000690, PB-000004)
- Answer the price worry with the paid pilot the client suggested. Start with three clinics, show value, then roll out to the rest. Compare value, not only price. (I000691, I000692, I000693, I000696, PB-000004, PB-000001)

Risks:
- The client is unhappy with the price and compares us with another vendor. A past diagnostics deal was lost to another vendor mainly on price. (I000691, PB-000004)
- The data storage question is open. In a past lost deal, a pending data answer was a reason for the loss. (I000690, PB-000004)
- The budget is INR 40 lakh. The deal value is INR 42 lakh, which is above it. Plan how to close this gap, for example with the pilot scope. (I000700, I000691)
- The target launch is 8 November. In a past healthcare deal the launch date moved later, to 20 November. Confirm what depends on the date and how firm it is. (I000698, PB-000001)
- Scope can grow after the pilot. Twelve clinics need staff training at each clinic. A past healthcare project added requirements late. (I000688, I000699, PB-000001)

Ask at kickoff:
- Where must the data be stored? (I000690, PB-000004)
- Will users need to upload insurance claims, and who checks them? (PB-000001)
- Which lab or external systems must the app connect to? (PB-000001)
- Which languages must the screens support, for example Hindi? (PB-000001)
- Is there a fixed launch date, and what depends on it? (I000698, PB-000001)
- Which channel for reminders: SMS or WhatsApp? (PB-000001)
- Which reports or dashboards does the client need, and how often? (PB-000001)

lines.raw: Hi everyone, shall we begin? Nandini ji, aap sun rahe ho?
lines.clean: Hi everyone, shall we begin? Nandini ji, can you hear us?

lines.raw: Haan Akbar, bilkul. Pehle ek update, doctors ne beta app try kiya, feedback achha hai.
lines.clean: Yes Akbar, absolutely. First, an update: the doctors tried the beta app, and the feedback is good.

lines.raw: Great. Next kya hum launch ki date finalize karein?
lines.clean: Great. Next, shall we finalize the launch date?

lines.raw: Hum chahte hain ki pehle clinic ka launch six November ko ho.
lines.clean: We want the clinic launch to happen first, on 6 November.

lines.raw: Aur haan, Hindi screens abhi bhi baaki hain, woh to chahiye hi.
lines.clean: And yes, the Hindi screens are still pending. We definitely need those.

lines.raw: Hindi ke liye translations aap bhejoge?
lines.clean: Will you send the translations for Hindi?

lines.raw: Achha, ek aur cheez, insurance claim wala flow kaisa chal raha hai?
lines.clean: Okay, one more thing: how is the insurance claim flow going?

lines.raw: Wo theek hai, uh, test mein hai abhi.
lines.clean: It is fine. It is in testing right now.

lines.raw: Aur reminders ka kya karna hai, matlab kaunsa channel?
lines.clean: And what should we do about reminders, I mean, which channel?

lines.raw: Matlab patients WhatsApp use karte hain zyada.
lines.clean: I mean, patients use WhatsApp more.

lines.raw: Haan, SMS toh koi dekhta hi nahi.
lines.clean: Yes, nobody looks at SMS at all.

lines.raw: Hum decide karte hain: WhatsApp se hi reminders jayenge.
lines.clean: We decide: reminders will go only by WhatsApp.

lines.raw: Done, note kar liya. Thanks everyone.

live_call_summary.what: End summary of live call LC02 (Akbar, CSM)
live_call_summary.final_text: Akbar Ali spoke with Nandini of MedBridge Clinics. Nandini said all is going fine and the doctors like the app. She raised one open point: the WhatsApp approval has not come, so the clinic wants to send reminders by SMS instead. Akbar said he will think about it and come back after the sync. Nandini said there is no hurry. Until then, the clinic will show the demo to the doctors. One conflict to note: on Sep 30 Akbar agreed in a call that reminders go by WhatsApp only. The SMS idea changes that decision. No new decision was made on this call.
next_steps: Akbar: after the sync, reply to Nandini on whether reminders move from WhatsApp to SMS.
Akbar: check the Sep 30 decision (reminders by WhatsApp only) and ask the client directly if that decision changes.
Akbar: find out the status of the WhatsApp approval and when it might come.
Do not record SMS as the new decision until Akbar and the client confirm it.
Nandini's team: continue to show the demo to the doctors.

{"answer": "Trip totals: trip TR005 left on 2026-08-08 for Pune (customer success). It cost 9150 INR. The trip check lists its cost as 8700 INR, and the books do not say why the two differ. This is 1 trip, and it had a cheaper option.
Savings: yes, TR005 was too expensive. The rule is same city trips. Trip TR004 also went to Pune on 2026-08-05. The cheaper option cost 4700 INR. The saving is 4450 INR.
Policy suggestions:
1. Before booking a trip, check for another trip to the same city in the same week.
2. Ask teams to combine same city trips, or share the booking, when dates are close.
3. Ask for a short reason when two trips to one city happen within a few days."}
